record.original_question: Is every infinite almost radically closed field ample, where almost radically closed means that for every positive integer n the subgroup of n-th powers has finite index in K^times?

evidence.quote: Call K almost radically closed if for every n the subgroup of n-th powers has finite index in Ktimes.
One could strengthen the above question and ask whether every infinite almost radically closed field is ample.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A field $K$ is called ample (also known as large) if every smooth $K$-curve $C$ with at least one $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points; equivalently, $K$ is existentially closed in the Laurent series field $K((t))$. Call a field $K$ almost radically closed if for every positive integer $n$ the subgroup $(K^{\times})^{n}$ of $n$-th powers has finite index in the multiplicative group $K^{\times}$.

Question: Is every infinite almost radically closed field ample?
